akhfash:7-7.t: He said ﴿خُشَّعاً﴾: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they come out of the graves humbled. Some read ﴿خاشِعا﴾ because it is an attribute placed first, so he treated it like the verb; its counterpart is ﴿خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ﴾.

akhfash:19-19.t: And He said ﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ﴾, and ﴿يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ﴾ as an attribute.

akhfash:24-24.t: And He said ﴿أَبَشَراً مِّنَّا وَاحِداً نَّتَّبِعُهُ﴾: He put "a human" in the accusative since the interrogative particle fell on it, and He made the verb fall on something connected with it.

akhfash:44-44.t: And He said ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُّنتَصِرٌ﴾ ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ﴾: He gave the group a single back in the wording. And He said ﴿وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَاذِرُونَ﴾, and He said ﴿لاَ يَرْتَدُّ إِلَيْهِمْ طَرْفُهُمْ﴾.

akhfash:48-49.t:
And He said ﴿ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾ ﴿إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ﴾: He made the touch something tasted, by the latitude of speech; it is said: "How did you find the taste of the beating?" This is figurative (majāz). As for the accusative of ﴿كلّ﴾, it is in the dialect of those who say "عبدَ اللهِ ضَرَبْتُه" (ʿAbd Allāh, I struck him), and that is frequent in the speech of the Arabs. "كلُّ" has also been put in the nominative, in the dialect of those who use the nominative, and in another way as well.
He said ﴿إِنَّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ﴾ and made ﴿خَلَقْنَاهُ﴾ an attribute of "thing".

akhfash:53-53.t: And He said ﴿وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُّسْتَطَرٌ﴾: He made the khabar (predicate) singular, for "all".

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَانْشَقَّ الْقَمَرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يَرَوْا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, in is conditional, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿آيَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿يُعْرِضُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis. ﴿وَيَقُولُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يعرضوا. ﴿سِحْرٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ an adjective of سحر; the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَكَذَّبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to كذبوا. ﴿أَهْواءَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and a mubtadaʾ (subject); أمر is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) and مستقر is the khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿مِنَ الْأَنْباءِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿مُزْدَجَرٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿حِكْمَةٌ﴾ a badal (substitute) from mā, and بالغة is an adjective of حكمة. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and mā is negating. ﴿تُغْنِ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿النُّذُرُ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿فَتَوَلَّ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition that does not govern the jussive and has no grammatical position. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿يَدْعُ الدَّاعِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلى شَيْءٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿نُكُرٍ﴾ an adjective of شيء.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿خُشَّعاً أَبْصارُهُمْ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), and أبصارهم is the fāʿil (agent) of خشعا. ﴿يَخْرُجُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ kaʾanna and its noun. ﴿جَرادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate), and منتشر is an adjective of جراد; the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِلَى الدَّاعِ﴾ the two (preposition and genitive noun) are attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them. ﴿يَقُولُ الْكافِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿هذا يَوْمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿عَسِرٌ﴾ an adjective of يوم; the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and an adverb of time. ﴿قَوْمُ﴾ its fāʿil (agent). ﴿نُوحٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَكَذَّبُوا عَبْدَنا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to كذبوا. ﴿مَجْنُونٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَازْدُجِرَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿فَدَعا رَبَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ﴾ anna, its noun and its khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna and what follows it is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿فَانْتَصِرْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition that does not govern the jussive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فَفَتَحْنا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَبْوابَ﴾ its mafʿūl (object). ﴿السَّماءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِماءٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مُنْهَمِرٍ﴾ an adjective of ماء; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَفَجَّرْنَا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ its mafʿūl (object). ﴿عُيُوناً﴾ tamyīz (specification); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَالْتَقَى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فجرنا. ﴿الْماءُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿عَلى أَمْرٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿قُدِرَ﴾ a passive past verb; the clause is an adjective of أمر.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَحَمَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلى ذاتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَلْواحٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَدُسُرٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ألواح.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿بِأَعْيُنِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿جَزاءً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ the two are attached to جزاء. ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent. ﴿كُفِرَ﴾ a passive past verb; the clause كفر is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the clause كان كفر is the ṣila (relative clause) of man and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ see verse no. 4 of this same sura. ﴿تَرَكْناها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl (object). ﴿آيَةً﴾ its second mafʿūl; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and hal is a particle of interrogation. ﴿مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ genitive in form by the redundant (zāʾida) min, nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and kayfa is an interrogative noun, the advanced khabar (predicate) of kāna. ﴿كانَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿عَذابِي﴾ its noun. ﴿وَنُذُرِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to عذابي.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ its i'rab has preceded in verse 4 of the sura. ﴿يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِلذِّكْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾ its i'rab has preceded in verse 15 of the sura.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ عادٌ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾: its i'rab has preceded in verse 16 of the sura.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿رِيحاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿صَرْصَراً﴾ an adjective of ريحا; the clause أرسلنا.. is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause إنا.. is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي يَوْمِ﴾ the two are attached to أرسلنا. ﴿نَحْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُسْتَمِرٍّ﴾ an adjective of نحس.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿تَنْزِعُ النَّاسَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is an adjective of ريحا. ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ﴾ kaʾanna, its noun and its khabar (predicate). ﴿نَخْلٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾ an adjective of أعجاز; the clause كأنهم.. is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:21-22.t: Their i'rab has been given before.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿فَقالُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَبَشَراً﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation, and بشرا is accusative (manṣūb) by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb). ﴿مِنَّا﴾ an adjective of بشرا. ﴿واحِداً﴾ an adjective of بشرا. ﴿نَتَّبِعُهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّا إِذاً﴾ inna and its noun, and idhan is a particle of answer and requital. ﴿لَفِي﴾ the lām, and the shifted (al-muzaḥlaqa). [Translator's note: so in the source, «اللام والمزحلقة»; meant is "the shifted lām".] ﴿في ضَلالٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ضلال. The clause إنا.. is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿أَأُلْقِيَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation, and a passive past verb. ﴿الذِّكْرُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِنا﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and transition. ﴿هُوَ كَذَّابٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿أَشِرٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿سَيَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the sīn is a particle of futurity, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿غَداً﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿الْأَشِرُ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of يعلمون.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw, the nūn being dropped for the annexation. ﴿النَّاقَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) فتنة. ﴿فَارْتَقِبْهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and an imperative verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاصْطَبِرْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ارتقبهم; the nominal clause is also the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿وَنَبِّئْهُمْ﴾ an imperative verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنَّ الْماءَ قِسْمَةٌ﴾ anna, its noun and its khabar (predicate). ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from anna and what follows it stands in place of the second and third objects of نبئ. ﴿كُلُّ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to شرب. ﴿شِرْبٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُحْتَضَرٌ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿فَنادَوْا صاحِبَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, and the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿فَتَعاطى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿فَعَقَرَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تعاطى; the two verbal clauses are conjoined to what precedes them.

daas-irab:30-30.t: Its i'rab has preceded in verse 16 of the sura.

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَرْسَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿صَيْحَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿واحِدَةً﴾ an adjective of صيحة; the clause إنا أرسلنا is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَكانُوا﴾ a conjunction, and kāna and its noun. ﴿كَهَشِيمِ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar of kāna. ﴿الْمُحْتَظِرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:32-32.t: See verse no. 17 of the sura.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لُوطٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿حاصِباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿آلَ﴾ excepted (mustathnā) by illā, annexed to لوط. ﴿لُوطٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿نَجَّيْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِسَحَرٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause إنا أرسلنا.. is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿نِعْمَةً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نعمة. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿نَجْزِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). [Translator's note: the source vowels the word as مِنْ; the Quranic word is the relative noun ﴿مَنْ﴾.] ﴿شَكَرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of man.

daas-irab:36-36.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ see verse 4. ﴿أَنْذَرَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿بَطْشَتَنا﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَتَمارَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِالنُّذُرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿راوَدُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فَطَمَسْنا أَعْيُنَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾ a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عَذابِي﴾ its mafʿūl. ﴿وَنُذُرِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to عذابي; the clause is the object of an omitted saying.

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿صَبَّحَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿بُكْرَةً﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾ an adjective of عذاب; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:39-40.t: The i'rab of the two verses has preceded.

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿جاءَ آلَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿النُّذُرُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:42-42.t: ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كُلِّها﴾ tawkīd (emphasis); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَأَخَذْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَخْذَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), annexed to عزيز. ﴿عَزِيزٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُقْتَدِرٍ﴾ an adjective of عزيز.

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿أَكُفَّارُكُمْ خَيْرٌ﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ أُولئِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ an advanced khabar. ﴿بَراءَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي الزُّبُرِ﴾ the two are attached to براءة; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿مُنْتَصِرٌ﴾ an adjective of جميع.

daas-irab:45-45.t: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ﴾ the sīn is for futurity, and a passive imperfect verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَيُوَلُّونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الدُّبُرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿بَلِ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿السَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَالسَّاعَةُ أَدْهى﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَمَرُّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:47-47.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ضلال; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ﴾ an adverb of time, and a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فِي النَّارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿ذُوقُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of an implied (muqaddar) saying. ﴿مَسَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to سقر. ﴿سَقَرَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:49-49.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, annexed to شيء. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿خَلَقْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿بِقَدَرٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the verbal clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) and has no grammatical position, and the implied verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna.

daas-irab:50-50.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is negating. ﴿أَمْرُنا﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿واحِدَةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿كَلَمْحٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِالْبَصَرِ﴾ the two are attached to لمح; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:51-51.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿أَهْلَكْنا أَشْياعَكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ﴾: see verse 16. [Translator's note: so in the source; the i'rab of this phrase was given under verse 15.]

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿وَكُلُّ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَعَلُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is an adjective of شيء; and ﴿فِي الزُّبُرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:53-53.t: ﴿وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَكَبِيرٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to صغير. ﴿مُسْتَطَرٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:54-54.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿وَنَهَرٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:55-55.t: ﴿فِي مَقْعَدِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from His words في جنات. ﴿صِدْقٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place, annexed to مليك. ﴿مَلِيكٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُقْتَدِرٍ﴾ an adjective of مليك.

farraa:1-1.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَٱنشَقَّ ٱلْقَمَرُ﴾. It has been mentioned that it split, and that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd saw (Mount) Ḥirāʾ between its two halves, the two halves of the moon.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن يَرَوْاْ آيَةً...﴾ — He means the moon — ﴿يُعْرِضُواْ وَيَقُولُواْ سِحْرٌ مُّسْتَمِرٌّ﴾.
That is: it will come to nothing and pass away.
Some of them said: magic, part of which resembles another.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكُلُّ أَمْرٍ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ﴾.
The outcome of their denial will settle, and the outcome of the saying of those who believe, until they know its reality through punishment and reward.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿حِكْمَةٌ بَالِغَةٌ﴾.
It is nominative as conjoined to (ما فيه مُزْدجَر), and (ما) is in the position of a nominative. Had you made it nominative as a new sentence (istiʾnāf), as though you were explaining (ما) by it, it would have been correct; and had it been accusative by «qaṭʿ» (detachment, i.e. as ḥāl), since it is indefinite while «ما» is definite, it would have been correct.
Similar to it in its being nominative is: ﴿هذا ما لدىَّ عتيدٌ﴾; had (عتيدٌ) been accusative, it would have been correct. And His saying: ﴿فَمَا تُغْنِ ٱلنُّذُرُ﴾.
If you wish, you make (ما) a negation, meaning: the warnings do not avail them; and if you wish, you put it in the position of «أىّ», as though you said: what then do the warnings avail? [187/ا]

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿خُشَّعاً أَبْصَارُهُمْ﴾.
When the verb (here, the participle) comes before a feminine noun to which it belongs, or before a feminine plural such as «الأبصار», «الأعمار» and the like, it is permissible to make the verb feminine, masculine, or plural. All of that has come in this word: Ibn ʿAbbās read it (خاشعاً).
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told me:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Hushaym and Abū Muʿāwiya told me, from Wāʾil ibn Dāwūd, from Muslim ibn Yasār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read it (خاشعاً).
[Muḥammad told me:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Hushaym told me, from ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī, from al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī, that one of them said (خاشعاً) and the other (خُشَّعاً).
Al-Farrāʾ said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (خاشِعةً أبصارُهُم), and the reading of the people since is (خُشعاً أبصارُهم).
The poet said:
وشبَابٍ حَسنٍ أوجُهُهُمْ * من إياد بن نزار نب مَعَدِّ
(And many a youth whose faces are fair, of Iyād son of Nizār son of Maʿadd.)
And another said:
يرمى الفِجاجَ الركبانُ مُعترضاً * أعناقَ بُزَّلِهَا مُرْخًى لها الجدُلُ
(The riders cast at the mountain passes, the necks of their full-grown camels stretched across, their reins slackened for them.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: «الجدُل» is the plural of «الجَديل», which is the halter. Had he said «مُعترضاتٍ» or «مُعترضةً» it would have been correct, and (likewise) «مُرْخاةً» and «مرخياتٍ».
«[Translator's note: «نب» in the verse is as printed, evidently for «بن».]»

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿مُّهْطِعِينَ﴾: looking towards the caller.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَجْنُونٌ وَٱزْدُجِرَ﴾.
He was rebuked with insults. «ازْدُجِر» is the iftaʿala form from «زَجَرْتُ». When a word begins with zāy, the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form becomes dāl in it; of this are «زُجِرَ», «ازْدُجِرَ» and «مُزْدَجَرٌ», and of this also «المُزْدَلِف» and «يزداد», which are from the verb (pattern) «يَفتعِل»; so make analogy on this for whatever occurs.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿فَالْتَقَى ٱلمَآءُ عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾.
He meant the two waters: the water of the earth and the water of the sky. «التقاء» (meeting) is only possible for two nouns or more; it was only permissible with «الماء» because «الماء» can be plural and singular.
And His saying: ﴿عَلَىٰ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾: decreed in the Mother of the Book.
It is said: it had been determined that the amount of the two waters was one. And it is said: it had been decreed for what Allah intended of punishing them.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَحَمَلْنَاهُ﴾.
We carried Noah on (a thing) of planks, meaning the ship; ﴿وَدُسُرٍ﴾: the nails of the ship and its cords by which it is bound.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿جَزَآءً لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ﴾.
That is: (one who) was denied.
He is saying: We did to him and to them what We did as a recompense for what was done to Noah and his companions. He said «لِمَنْ» meaning the people, and it has the sense of «ما». Do you not see that you say: «غُرّقوا لنوحٍ» (they were drowned for Noah) and «لِما صُنعَ بنُوح» (for what was done to Noah), and the meaning is one?

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ تَّرَكْنَاهَا آيَةً﴾.
He is saying: We preserved it after Noah as a sign.
And His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ﴾.
The meaning is «مُذتَكرٍ». When you form «مُفْتعل» from a word whose first letter is dhāl, the dhāl and the tāʾ of iftiʿāl become a doubled dāl. Some of Banū Asad say «مُذّكرٌ»: they let the dhāl prevail, so it becomes a doubled dhāl.
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Kisāʾī told me — [and by Allah, I have known him to be nothing but truthful] — from Isrāʾīl and al-Qarzamī, from Abū Isḥāq, from al-Aswad ibn Yazīd, who said: We said to ʿAbd Allāh: «فهلم من مُذَّكرٍ» or «مُدَّكرٍ»? He said: The Messenger of Allah [187/ب] ﷺ taught me to recite: (مُدَّكِرٌ) with dāl.
«[Translator's note: «فهلم» is as printed, evidently for «فهل».]»

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ﴾.
«النذر» here is a maṣdar (verbal noun), its meaning being: how then was My warning? Similar to it is ﴿عذراً أو نذراً﴾ (15); both are pronounced light (with sukūn) and heavy (with ḍamma), as He said ﴿إلى شَىء نُّكُرٍ﴾, which is heavy in "اقتربت" (al-Qamar) and light in the shorter Sūrat al-Nisāʾ, where it was said "نُكْراً".
«[Translator's note: «(15)» is as in the source; ﴿عذراً أو نذراً﴾ is Q 77:6.]»

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ﴾.
He is saying: We made it easy; were it not for that, the servants would not have been able to utter the speech of Allah. And it is said: «ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر» means for memorising; for there is no book that is memorised by heart other than it.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ﴾: it continued upon them with its ill-omen.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ﴾: their lower parts. «منقعر» means the felled palm tree.

farraa:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّآ إِذاً لَّفِي ضَلاَلٍ وَسُعُرٍ﴾. By «السُّعُر» He meant hardship, (as) of punishment.

farraa:25-26.t:
His saying: ﴿كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ﴾: Mujāhid alone read «الأَشُر».
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna told me, from a man, from Mujāhid, that he read (سَيَعْلَمُونَ) with yāʾ — so Sufyān said — ﴿مَّنِ ٱلْكَذَّابُ ٱلأَشِرُ﴾. It is like your saying in speech: «رجل حَذِر» and «حَذُرٌ» (wary), «فطِنٌ» and «فطُنٌ» (astute), «عجِل» and «عَجُلٌ» (hasty).
[Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl told me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he read «سيعلمون غدا» with yāʾ.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾.
The she-camel has a day and they have a day; so He said «بينهم», (meaning) between them and the she-camel.
And His saying: ﴿كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُّحْتَضَرٌ﴾: its owners and whoever is entitled to it attend it.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿فَكَانُواْ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ﴾.
(The one) who fences in over his dry stubble. Al-Ḥasan alone read «كهشيم المحتظَر», with a fatḥa on the ẓāʾ, thus making «الهشيم» the muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) to «المحتظَر»; it is as He said: ﴿إِنَّ هذا لهو حقُّ اليقين﴾, where «الحق» is «اليقين»; and as He said: ﴿ولَدَارُ الآخِرةِ خَيْرٌ﴾, putting «الدار» in construct with «الآخرة», while it is the Hereafter itself. «الهشيم» is trees (and plants) when they dry up.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿نَّجَّيْنَاهُم بِسَحَرٍ﴾.
«سحر» here is fully declined (with nunation), because it is indefinite, as in your saying «نجيناهم بليلٍ» (We saved them by night). But when the Arabs drop the bāʾ from it, they do not decline it, and say: «فعلت هذا سحرَ يا هذا» (I did this at daybreak, you there). It is as though, in their not declining it, their speech had it with the article al-, and it ran on that basis; so when the alif and lām were dropped while they were still intended, it was not declined. The speech of the Arabs is to say «ما زال عندنا مذ السحر» (he has been with us since daybreak); they hardly say anything else.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَتَمَارَوْاْ بِٱلنُّذُرِ﴾: they denied what he told them.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهُم بُكْرَةً عَذَابٌ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ﴾: The Arabs decline «غدوة» and «بكرة» fully and also leave them undeclined; most usage with «غدوة» is to leave it undeclined, and most usage with «بكرة» is that it is declined.
He said: I heard one of them say: «أتيته بكرةَ باكرا» (I came to him early in the morning). Whoever does not decline it makes it definite, because it is a noun that always refers to one (fixed) time, like «أمس» (yesterday) and «غد» (tomorrow). The Arabs most often decline «غدوة» when it is paired with «عشية», saying: «إنى لآتيك غُدوةً وعشيةً» (I shall come to you morning and evening), and some of them say «غدوةً وعشيةَ»; and some of them do not decline «عشية» [188/ا] because of how often it has accompanied «غدوة».
«[Translator's note: «تجريمها» in the source is evidently a misprint for «تجريهما» (decline them).]»
And His saying: ﴿عَذَابٌ مُّسْتَقِرٌّ﴾.
He is saying: a punishment that is real.

farraa:43-45.t:
His saying: ﴿أَكُفَّارُكُمْ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أُوْلَئِكُمْ﴾.
He is saying: are your disbelievers, O people of Mecca, better than these whom the punishment struck, or do you have an immunity in the Scriptures? He is saying: or do you have an immunity from the punishment? Then He said: «أم يقولون», that is: «أيقولون» (do they say): we are a great host, victorious? So Allah said: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ﴾, and that was the day of Badr.
He said «الدبر» in the singular and did not say «الأدبار»; all of it is permissible. It is correct to say «ضربْنا منهم الرءوس والأعين» (we struck their heads and eyes) and «ضربنا منهم الرأس واليد» (we struck their head and hand); and it is as you say «إنه لكثير الدينار والدرهم» (he has much dinar and dirham), meaning dinars and dirhams.

farraa:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدْهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ﴾. He is saying: more grievous for them than the punishment of the day of Badr; and «أمرّ» is from «المرارة» (bitterness).

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "يوم يسحبون إلى النار على وجوههم".
And His saying: ﴿ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾. «سقر» is one of the names of Hell; it is not declined (a diptote). Every name of a feminine, whether it has the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) or does not have the hāʾ, is declined, except particular names that are light, and so were declined, while some left them undeclined; these are «هند», «دعد», «جُمل» and «رئم»: they are declined and not declined. Whoever does not decline them says: every feminine's due is not to be declined, because it has the sense of the hāʾ, even if it does not appear; do you not see that when you form its diminutive you say «هنيدة» and «دعيدة»? Whoever declines them says: they became light because of the quiescence of their middle letter, and the hāʾ was dropped and did not appear, so they became light and were declined.
«[Translator's note: «فهو يجرى» (is declined) is as printed; the argument requires «فهو لا يجرى» (is not declined).]»

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَمْرُنَآ إِلاَّ وَاحِدَةٌ﴾, that is: a single time. This is about the Hour: like the twinkling of a flash.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وَكَبِيرٍ مُّسْتَطَرٌ﴾. He means: every sin, small or great, is written down.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَهَرٍ﴾: its meaning is «أنهار» (rivers), and in its manner it is like His saying: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُولُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ (45). Al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard the Arabs say: «أتينا فلاناً فكنّا في لحمةٍ ونبيذة» (we came to so-and-so and were amid meat and date-wine), using the singular while the meaning is plenty.
And it is said: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَهَرٍ﴾ means in light and spaciousness. I heard one of the Arabs recite:
إِن تك ليليا فإنى نَهِرُ * متى أرى الصبح فلا أنتظرُ
(If you are a man of the night, I am a man of the day; when I see the morning I do not wait.)
The meaning of «نَهِر» is: a person of the day (nahār). It has been transmitted: "وما أمْرُنا إلاَّ وَحدةً" in the accusative; it is as though he implied a verb by which «الواحدة» is made accusative, as you say to a man: «ما أنت إلا ثيابَك مرة، ودابتك مرة، ورأسك مرة» (you are nothing but your clothes one time, your mount another, and your head another), that is: you attend to that.
Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say: «إنما العامرى عِمَّتَه» (the ʿĀmirī is nothing but his turban), that is: he attends to nothing of his clothing but the turban. Al-Farrāʾ said: and I do not like the accusative of it in recitation.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Qamar
Meccan
﷽
﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾: the exegetes are agreed — and we have narrated it from trustworthy people of knowledge — that the moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Abū Isḥāq «[Translator's note: i.e. al-Zajjāj himself.]» said: A group who have strayed from the right course and from what the people of knowledge hold claimed that its interpretation is that the moon will split on the Day of Resurrection. But the matter is clear from the wording and from the consensus of the people of knowledge, because of His saying: ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2] — so how could this be at the Resurrection?
Abū Isḥāq said — and all that is dictated to you on this is what Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq narrated to me — he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Minhāl narrated to us, he said: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas: «that the people of Mecca asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign, so he showed them the moon twice — its splitting», and he used to mention this hadith at this verse: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾. Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, he said: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from Qatāda, from Anas, who said: "The moon split into two parts."
Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Ḥirmī ibn ʿUmāra narrated to us, he said: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Qatāda, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪd «[Translator's note: so in the source; possibly a misprint for Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd.]» narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda, from Anas, who said: «"The people of Mecca asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign, and the moon split in Mecca twice, and He said: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]"», meaning: passing away. Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Naṣr narrated to us, he said: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, he said: Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "The moon split, and I saw the mountain between the two gaps of the moon." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Naṣr narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: Isrāʾīl informed us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from al-Aswad, from ʿAbd Allāh — concerning His saying ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ — he said: "The moon split until I saw the mountain between the two halves of the moon." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Numayr narrated to us, he said: Abū Muʿāwiya narrated to us, he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: «"The moon split while we were with the Prophet ﷺ at Minā, until one part of it went behind the mountain, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Musaddad narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba and Sufyān, from al-Aʿmash, and from Ibrāhīm, from Abū Maʿmar, from Abū Masʿūd, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Prophet ﷺ into two parts, one part above the mountain and one part below it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Masʿūd «[Translator's note: so in the source; the parallel chains have Musaddad.]» narrated to us, he said: Yaḥyā narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Aʿmash, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿUmar, the like of it. Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abī Najīḥ informed us, from Mujāhid, from Ibn Abī Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two pieces, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: 'Bear witness, bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī said — and he narrated it to us another time — from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, from Abū Maʿmar, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: «"The moon split into two pieces, so that we saw it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: 'Bear witness.'"» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Kathīr narrated to us, from Sulaymān — meaning Ibn Kathīr — from Ḥuṣayn, from Muḥammad ibn Jubayr, from his father, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two parts, on this mountain and on this mountain, and the people said: 'Muḥammad has bewitched us.' A man said: 'If he has bewitched you, he has not bewitched all the people.'"» And Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, he said: Zuhayr ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Dāwūd, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Three things that Allah has mentioned in the Qurʾān have already come to pass: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ — the moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ into two pieces, so that the people saw it." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Naṣr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, he said: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās — concerning His saying ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ — he said: "It happened before the Hijra: the moon split, so that they saw its two pieces." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr said, from ʿIkrima, who said: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the idolaters said: 'The moon has been bewitched, the moon has been bewitched!' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]."» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr narrated to us, he said: al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrima: «"The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the idolaters said: 'The moon has been bewitched, the moon has been bewitched!' So there came down: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ ﴿وَإنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا ويَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 2]."» Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿĀrim ibn al-Faḍl and Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, they said: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib «[Translator's note: so in the source; the name ʿIkrima in this chain looks out of place.]», from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, who said: "I set out with my father on Friday, and Ḥudhayfa addressed us — and Sulaymān said in his narration: Ḥudhayfa gave the sermon while he was at al-Madāʾin — and he recited ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾, then said: 'Indeed, the Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. Indeed, today is the training ground and tomorrow the race.'" Sulaymān said in his narration: "So I said to my father: 'O father, will the horses be set loose tomorrow?!'" And ʿĀrim said in his narration: "So I said to my father: 'Will the people race tomorrow?!' When the following Friday came, he addressed us and recited ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ and said: 'Indeed, the Hour has drawn near, and the moon split in the time of your Prophet ﷺ. Indeed, today is the training ground and tomorrow the race; the goal is the Fire, and the winner is the one who races to Paradise.'" Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl narrated to us, he said: Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥabīb, who said: "We were at al-Madāʾin and came to the Friday prayer, and Ḥudhayfa addressed us. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'To proceed: Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, says: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾. Indeed, today is the training ground and tomorrow the race; indeed, the goal is the Fire.' When the next Friday came, he addressed us; he praised Allah and extolled Him" — he said — "and said the like of what he had said, and said: 'The winner is the one who races to Paradise.'" Ismāʿīl narrated to us: ʿAlī narrated to us, he said: Sufyān narrated to us, from Sulaymān and Qaṭar «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably Fiṭr.]», from Muslim, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "The inescapable punishment (al-lizām) has passed, the great seizure (al-baṭsha) has passed, the smoke (al-dukhān) has passed, and al-Rūm (the Romans) has passed." Ismāʿīl narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾. Ibn Zayd said: "The moon split in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and half of it was seen on Quʿayqiʿān and the other half on Abū Qays «[Translator's note: i.e. Mount Abū Qubays, so written in the source.]»."

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying: ﴿فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ فانْتَصِرْ﴾: the reading is ﴿أنِّي﴾ with fatḥa on the alif, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar the grammarian read "إنِّي" with kasra on the alif. Sībawayh explained "إنِّي" with kasra, saying: it is on the intention of "saying" (qawl), in the sense of: "So he called upon his Lord and said: 'I am overcome.'" He said: and similar to it is ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِهِ أوْلِياءَ ما نَعْبُدُهم إلا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إلى اللَّهِ زُلْفى﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]; the meaning is: "They said: 'We only worship them so that they may bring us near.'" And whoever reads with fatḥa — and that is the proper way — the meaning is: "He called upon his Lord with [the words] that I am overcome."

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying: ﴿فَفَتَحْنا أبْوابَ السَّماءِ بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ﴾: the meaning is: "So We answered his supplication and helped him." And He made clear the help with which he was helped, saying: ﴿فَفَتَحْنا أبْوابَ السَّماءِ بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ﴾: pouring down violently.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿وَفَجَّرْنا الأرْضَ عُيُونًا﴾: this is the majority reading, ﴿عُيُونًا﴾ with ḍamma; it has also been transmitted as "عِيُونًا", with kasra on the ʿayn, and that is poor in Arabic.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فالتَقى الماءُ عَلى أمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾: meaning the water of the sky and of the earth. He did not say "fa-ltaqā l-māʾāni" (the two waters met), though had it been so it would have been permissible; but "الماءُ" is a noun that comprises the water of the earth and the water of the sky. The meaning of ﴿عَلى أمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾ is: which had been decreed in the Preserved Tablet. And it has been said: "قَدْ قُدِرَ" means the amount of the sky's water was like the amount of the earth's water.

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿وَحَمَلْناهُ عَلى ذاتِ ألْواحٍ ودُسُرٍ﴾: the meaning is: "on a ship made of planks". "اَلدُّسُرُ" is the name for the nails and the cords with which the planks are bound. Everything like nailing, or driving one thing into another with force and great compulsion, is "دَسْرٌ"; one says "dasartu l-mismāra, adsuruhu, wa-adsiruhu" (I drove in the nail). "اَلدُّسُرُ": its singular is "دِسارٌ", like "حِمارٌ" and "حُمُرٌ".

zajjaj:14-14.t:
And His saying: ﴿لِمَن كانَ كُفِرَ﴾, that is: We did that as a recompense for Nūḥ and his companions, that is: We saved him and those who believed with him, and drowned those who denied him, as a recompense for what was done to him.
And His saying: ﴿تَجْرِي بِأعْيُنِنا﴾, that is: it sails within Our sight and under Our protection.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ تَرَكْناها آيَةً﴾, that is: We left this deed and the matter of Nūḥ's ship as a sign, that is: a mark from which a lesson may be taken. ﴿فَهَلْ مِن مُدَّكِرٍ﴾: the reading is with the undotted dāl. Its origin is "مُذْتَكِرٌ", with dhāl and tāʾ, but the tāʾ was replaced by dāl — and the dhāl is from the place of articulation of the tāʾ, and is closer to the dāl than to the tāʾ — and then the dhāl was assimilated into the dāl. This is the proper way, I mean the reading with the undotted dāl. Some Arabs said "مُذَّكِرٍ", with the dotted dhāl, assimilating the second into the first; but this is not the proper way — the proper way is assimilating the first into the second.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾, that is: passing away; and it has been said: lasting.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكُلُّ أمْرٍ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾: its interpretation is that the deeds of the people of the Fire become settled for them, and the deeds of the people of Paradise become settled for them.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَهم مِنَ الأنْباءِ ما فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ﴾: meaning of the reports of those who went before them and were destroyed for their denial. ﴿ما فِيهِ مُزْدَجَرٌ﴾, that is: that in which there is a restraint. You say: "nahaytuhu fa-ntahā" (I forbade him and he desisted) and "zajartuhu fa-zdajara" (I rebuked him and he refrained). The origin is "fa-ztajara", with tāʾ, but when the tāʾ comes after a zāy it is replaced by a dāl, as in "مُزْدانٌ", whose origin is "مُزْتانٌ", and likewise "مُزْتَجَرٌ". It was replaced by a dāl only because the tāʾ is a voiceless (mahmūs) letter and the zāy a voiced (majhūr) letter, so in place of the tāʾ there was substituted a voiced letter, namely dāl. This is understood only by one who has mastered the whole of Arabic, and it is at the end of the Book of Sībawayh. What should be said to the learner is: when you form "اِفْتَعَلَ" or "مُفْتَعَلٌ" from a root whose first letter is zāy, change the tāʾ into a dāl, as in "اِزْدَجَرَ" and "مُزْدَجَرٌ".

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حِكْمَةٌ بالِغَةٌ﴾: "حِكْمَةٌ" is nominative as a badal (substitute) for "ما"; the meaning is: "And there has come to them far-reaching wisdom." And if you wish, you may make "حِكْمَةٌ" nominative with "هُوَ" implied; the meaning is: "It is far-reaching wisdom."
And His saying: ﴿فَما تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ﴾: "ما" may be interrogative in form with the meaning of rebuke, so that the meaning is: "So what do the warnings avail?!", and its position would be accusative by "تُغْنِ". And it may be a negation, in the sense of: "So the warnings do not avail."

zajjaj:6-6.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهم يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدّاعِ إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾: the complete pause (waqf al-tamām) is at ﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾.
And His saying ﴿إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾: to what they used to deny of the resurrection. "So turn away from them; on the day [such-and-such happens]" as in the verse «[Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]». "يَوْمَ" is accusative by His saying ﴿يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الأجْداثِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 7]. As for the omission of the wāw from "يَدْعُ" in the written text, it is because it is dropped in pronunciation owing to the meeting of two quiescent letters, namely the wāw of "يَدْعُو" and the lām of "اَلدّاعِ"; so it was written as it is pronounced. As for "اَلدّاعِ", retaining the yāʾ in it is better, though omitting it is permissible, because the kasra indicates it.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خُشَّعًا أبْصارُهُمْ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "They come out of the graves, their eyes humbled." It has also been read "خاشِعًا أبْصارُهُمْ", and Ibn Masʿūd read "خاشِعَةً أبْصارُهُمْ". With active participles, when they precede a plural, you may use the singular, as in "خاشِعًا أبْصارُهُمْ"; you may use the singular with the feminine, because of the femininity of the group: "خاشِعَةً أبْصارُهُمْ"; and you may use the plural, as in "خُشَّعًا أبْصارُهُمْ". You say: "marartu bi-shubbānin ḥasanin awjuhuhum" (I passed by young men handsome of face), "ḥisānin awjuhuhum" and "ḥasanatin awjuhuhum". The poet said:
؎وَشَبابٍ حَسَنٍ أوْجُهُهم ∗∗∗ مِن إيادِ بْنِ نِزارِ بْنِ مَعَدِ
(And young men handsome of face, of Iyād son of Nizār son of Maʿadd.)

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ إلى الدّاعِ﴾ is also accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "They come out, their eyes humbled, مُهْطِعِينَ." The meaning of ﴿مُهْطِعِينَ﴾ is: staring, not lifting their eyes away.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
And His saying: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهم قَوْمُ نُوحٍ﴾, that is: the people of Nūḥ denied Nūḥ before your people, O Muḥammad.
﴿وَقالُوا مَجْنُونٌ وازْدُجِرَ﴾: and they said "He is mad", just as your people said of you, O Muḥammad ﷺ, and upon them all.
"وازْدُجِرَ": he was rebuked with abuse. We have already explained what there is in "مُزْدَجَرٌ" concerning the change of the tāʾ into a dāl; the origin of this is "وازْتُجِرَ".

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنا القُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ﴾: the meaning is "We have made it easy". And it has been said: the books of the followers of other religions — such as the Torah and the Gospel — are recited by their followers only by looking at the text, and they hardly memorise their books from beginning to end as the Qurʾān is memorised.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا﴾: "صَرْصَرًا" means intensely cold.
﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ﴾: meaning "نَحْسٍ" (ill-omened), and "مُسْتَمِرٍّ" means lasting in its ill omen. And it has been said: on a Wednesday at the end of the month that does not come round again.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَنْـزِعُ النّاسَ كَأنَّهم أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾: "كَأنَّهُمْ" here is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "It plucks the people out, resembling uprooted palm trees." Al-munqaʿir is that which is cut off from its roots; the wind would throw them down on their faces.
And His saying: ﴿مُنْقَعِرٍ﴾: "النَّخْلُ" (palm trees) is treated as masculine and feminine; one says "hādhā nakhlun" and "hādhihi nakhlun". So "مُنْقَعِرٌ" follows those who say "hādhā nakhlun"; and for those who say "hādhihi nakhlun", it is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أعْجازُ نَخْلٍ خاوِيَةٍ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 7].

zajjaj:23-23.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ﴾: "اَلنُّذُرُ" is the plural of "نَذِيرٌ" (warner).

zajjaj:24-24.t:
﴿فَقالُوا أبَشَرًا مِنّا واحِدًا نَتَّبِعُهُ﴾: "بَشَرًا" is accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb, which the overt one explains; the meaning is: "Shall we follow a human being?!"
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا إذًا لَفي ضَلالٍ وسُعُرٍ﴾: its meaning is: "Then we would indeed be in error and madness." One says "nāqatun masʿūra" (a crazed she-camel) when she has madness. And it may be in the sense of: "If we follow him, we are in error and in torment."

zajjaj:25-25.t: And His saying: ﴿بَلْ هو كَذّابٌ أشِرٌ﴾: "أشِرٌ" is in the sense of "بَطِرٌ" (insolent, arrogant). One says "ashira, yaʾsharu, asharan, fa-huwa ashirun", like "baṭira, yabṭaru, baṭaran, fa-huwa baṭirun".

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا مُرْسِلُو النّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ﴾: "فِتْنَةً" is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "We are sending the she-camel in order to try them", that is: to test them.

zajjaj:28-28.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَبِّئْهم أنَّ الماءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهم كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُحْتَضَرٌ﴾, that is: the water is divided between the she-camel and Thamūd: she has a day and they have a day. And this is its meaning: "Every drinking turn is attended: the people attend the drinking one day, and the she-camel attends one day."

zajjaj:29-29.t:
﴿فَنادَوْا صاحِبَهم فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ﴾: he used to be called "Aḥmar Thamūd" (the Red One of Thamūd) and "Uḥaymir Thamūd" (the little Red One of Thamūd). The Arabs err and make him "Aḥmar ʿĀd", and use him as a proverb for ill omen. Zuhayr said, describing a war:
؎فَتُنْتِجْ لَكم غِلْمانَ أشْأمُ كُلُّهم ∗∗∗ كَأحْمَرِ عادٍ ثُمَّ تُرْضِعْ فَتَفْطِمِ
(It will bear for you sons of ill omen, all of them like the Red One of ʿĀd; then it will suckle and wean.)
And the meaning of ﴿فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ﴾ is: he undertook the hamstringing of the she-camel, and he hamstrung her, and so attained what he wanted.

zajjaj:31-31.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةً واحِدَةً فَكانُوا كَهَشِيمِ المُحْتَظِرِ﴾, with kasra on the ẓāʾ; and it is also read "اَلْمُحْتَظَرِ", with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ. "اَلْهَشِيمُ" is leaves that have dried up, broken and crumbled; that is: they became like the dry stubble which the owner of the enclosure (al-ḥaẓīra) gathers, that is: it had reached the utmost dryness, to the point of being gathered to be burned. Whoever reads "اَلْمُحْتَظَرِ" with fatḥa on the ẓāʾ, it is a noun for the enclosure; the meaning is: "like the stubble of the place in which stubble is enclosed". And whoever reads ﴿المُحْتَظِرِ﴾ with kasra on the ẓāʾ, it is a reference to the one who gathers the stubble of firewood in the enclosure, for he is "اَلْمُحْتَظِرُ", because he is the agent.

zajjaj:34-34.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إلا آلَ لُوطٍ نَجَّيْناهم بِسَحَرٍ﴾: "سَحَرٍ", when it is indefinite, meaning some pre-dawn time or other, is declinable (fully inflected, munṣarif). You say: "ataytu Zaydan saḥaran mina l-asḥār" (I came to Zayd at a pre-dawn time). But if you mean the pre-dawn of your current day, you say: "ataytuhu li-saḥarin yā hādhā" «[Translator's note: so in the source, with nunation; given the point being made, the intended form is presumably diptote, li-saḥara.]» and "ataytuhu saḥara yā hādhā" (I came to him this pre-dawn, you there).

zajjaj:35-35.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿نِعْمَةً مِن عِنْدِنا﴾ is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "We saved them in order to bestow favour upon them." Had it been read "نِعْمَةٌ مِن عِنْدِنا" (nominative), it would be a valid way, and the meaning would be: "That is a favour from Us; Our saving them is a favour from Us." Abū Isḥāq said: But I know of no one who read it so, so do not read it so unless a sound transmission is established. Our teachers among the people of knowledge said: Reading (qirāʾa) is a followed practice (sunna muttabaʿa), and they do not hold that anyone may read according to what is permissible in Arabic if no sound transmission is established.

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ راوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ فَطَمَسْنا أعْيُنَهُمْ﴾: the people of Lūṭ tried to seduce Lūṭ away from his guests, who were the angels. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded Jibrīl, and he struck their eyes with his wings with a single stroke, took them away and effaced them, and they remained in the house blind and bewildered.

zajjaj:38-38.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَبَّحَهم بُكْرَةً عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ﴾: "بُكُرَةً" and "غُدْوَةً" (early morning), when they are indefinite, take nunation and are declinable; but when you mean by them the early morning of your current day, you do not make them declinable. So "بُكْرَةً" here is indefinite. Had it been read "بُكُرَةَ عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ" and "نَجَّيْناهم بِسَحَرَ نِعْمَةً مِن عِنْدِنا", both would have been permissible in Arabic, the meaning being "the early morning of their day" and "the pre-dawn of their day". But the indefinite, declinable form is better in this verse, and no transmission has been established that it was on such-and-such a day of such-and-such a month.

zajjaj:43-43.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أكُفّارُكم خَيْرٌ مِن أُولَئِكُمْ﴾, that is: are your disbelievers, O company of Arabs and those to whom the Prophet ﷺ was sent, better than those — that is, the disbelievers whose stories and destruction We have mentioned? ﴿أمْ لَكم بَراءَةٌ في الزُّبُرِ﴾, that is: or has it come to you in the scriptures that you are absolved of what would necessitate your ʿidāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the source (عداءكم, "enmity towards you"); possibly a misprint for عذابكم, "your punishment".]»?

zajjaj:44-44.t:
﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعٌ مُنْتَصِرٌ﴾: the meaning is: "Rather, do they say: 'We are a united host, victorious', and so presume upon strength and unity against you?!"
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He would destroy them from the very direction from which they reckoned on victory, and said: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed His Prophet, peace be upon him, that He would make him prevail over them and make His word the highest, saying: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]; and this defeat was on the day of Badr.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
And His saying: ﴿سَيُهْزَمُ الجَمْعُ ويُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ﴾: the meaning is "and they will turn their backs (al-adbār, plural)", as He said: ﴿وَإنْ يُقاتِلُوكم يُوَلُّوكُمُ الأدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 111]. Likewise is the meaning in His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُتَّقِينَ في جَنّاتٍ ونَهَرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 54]; the meaning is "in gardens and rivers". The singular noun indicates the plural, and is made to suffice for the plural. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl recited:
؎بِها جِيَفُ الحَسْرى فَأمّا عِظامُها ∗∗∗ فَبِيضٌ وأمّا جِلْدُها فَصَلِيبُ
(In it are the carcasses of exhausted camels: as for their bones, they are white, and as for their skin, it is hard.)
They mean "and as for their skins (julūduhā)". And he recited:
؎فِي حَلْقِكم عَظْمٌ وقَدْ شُجِينا
(In your throat is a bone, and we have choked.)
The meaning is: in your throats are bones. And as he said:
؎كُلُوا في بَعْضِ بَطْنِكم تَعِفُّوا ∗∗∗ فَإنَّ زَمانَكم زَمَنٌ خَمِيصٌ
(Eat with part of your belly and stay restrained, for your time is a time of hunger.)
The meaning is: "Eat with part of your bellies."

zajjaj:46-46.t: Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهم والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾, that is: the killing and captivity that befell them on the day of Badr do not lighten for them anything of the punishment of the Hereafter. So He said: ﴿والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾, that is: more severe. Every dāhiya (calamity) means the severe matter for which no remedy can be found. And the meaning of ﴿وَأمَرُّ﴾ is: more bitter than killing and captivity.

zajjaj:47-47.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ المُجْرِمِينَ في ضَلالٍ وسُعُرٍ﴾: it is in the exegesis that this verse was revealed concerning the Qadariyya.

zajjaj:48-48.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ في النّارِ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ ذُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ﴾: the meaning is: "It will be said to them: Taste the touch of Saqar."

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿إنّا كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ﴾, that is: everything We have created is decreed and written in the Preserved Tablet before it occurs. "كُلَّ شَيْءٍ" is accusative by an implied verb; the meaning is: "We have created everything; We created it by measure." This is indicated by ﴿وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ فَعَلُوهُ في الزُّبُرِ﴾ [al-Qamar: 52] ﴿وَكُلُّ صَغِيرٍ وكَبِيرٍ مُسْتَطَرٌ﴾ [al-Qamar: 53]. "مُسْتَطَرٌ" is a passive participle from "اَلسَّطْرُ" (writing in lines); the meaning is: "Every sin, small and great, is recorded — written against those who do it before they do it, and written for them and against them when they do it, so that they may be recompensed for their deeds."
